newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weakens marginally vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weakens marginally vs dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened marginally against the dollar amid poor and cautious activity, commercial bank dealers said on Monday.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 59.21 against the dollar from 59.17 on Friday. On the pound, the shilling was posted at a mean rate of 99.33 from 98.90.
"Today is very slow. The shilling is stuck, trading within very narrow ranges," one forex dealer said.

Dealers said that while political tension in the country -- which upset the market and sent the shilling tumbling on a wave of panic-buying by foreign investors two weeks ago -- had eased, investors were still treading cautiously.
"Demand has eased. They (foreign investors) are no longer panicky but they're still watching," a dealer said.
Another dealer added: "It looks like the shilling is going to remain around here. Dollars from coffee and tea are very low. It's also a low season for horticulture."
Meanwhile the money market was liquid. Overnight rates were quoted at 5-8 percent compared to 5-11 percent on Friday.
